key_insight: Materials GNNs can reach similar final accuracy with very different amounts of trainable parameter-space freedom, so optimization-space demand is a meaningful metric beyond endpoint error.
engineering_relevance: Random-subspace intrinsic-dimension analysis gives practitioners a stress test for model robustness, showing which architectures and property tasks need more trainable capacity to learn reliably.
method: Train CGCNN, ALIGNN, and DimeNet++ in random parameter subspaces of increasing dimension.
Measure how predictive performance recovers as more independent trainable degrees of freedom are restored.
Compare recovery curves across six materials-property tasks, plus dataset-size and width sweeps.
evidence_signal: Across six tasks, metallic classification and log-bulk-modulus recovered near-reference performance from small subspaces, while phonon prediction was most sensitive; band-gap and formation-energy showed stronger architecture dependence.
watch_item: Random-subspace recovery is informative but depends on the chosen subspace sampling and training setup, so threshold values should not be treated as universal constants.
paper_title: Measuring trainable degrees of freedom in materials graph neural networks: a random-subspace intrinsic dimension analysis
